sections.label: Deaths of full-time National Servicemen
sections.summary: The House offers condolences to families of 3SG Gavin Chan, CFC Dave Lee and SCDF CPL Kok Yuen Chin.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Especially painful is when young National Servicemen who are serving their full-time NS, die.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: This House offers our deepest condolences to the families of 3SG Gavin Chan, CFC Dave Lee and, from the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF), CPL Kok Yuen Chin.

sections.label: Commanders' responsibility for NS training safety
sections.summary: Commanders recognise their responsibility to keep every serviceman safe during NS training, striving for zero training deaths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Commanders on the ground fully recognise this heavy responsibility of keeping every son of Singapore safe during their NS training, whether it is in the two years that they come full-time for intensive training, or each time that they are called after that.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: We must strive hard for zero training deaths because any death is one too many.

sections.label: Terrex and armoured vehicle speeds
sections.summary: Terrexes can move at 100 kilometre per hour and armoured vehicles at 70 kilometre per hour.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Our Terrexes can move at 100 kilometre per hour.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Our armoured vehicles can move at 70 kilometre per hour.

sections.label: Deaths of Gavin Chan and Dave Lee
sections.summary: 3SG Gavin Chan died in September last year when his Bionix rolled over, and CFC Dave Lee died in April from heat stroke complications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In September last year, 3SG Gavin Chan died when the Bionix vehicle he commanded rolled over.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: And in April this year, CFC Dave Lee died from complications of a heat stroke.

sections.label: Queensland coroner's report on 3SG Chan
sections.summary: The Queensland coroner's report on 3SG Chan's death is distributed to Members, with post-mortem findings redacted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Speaker, with your permission, I would now like to ask the Clerk to distribute the report from the Queensland coroner.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This report from the coroner was provided to 3SG Chan's parents. 3SG Chan's parents have given us permission for it to be distributed to Members of this House, except for the post-mortem findings which are redacted out of respect for the privacy of 3SG Chan and his family.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The Queensland coroner’s report provides the circumstances leading to the death of 3SG Chan as a result of multiple injuries sustained from motor vehicle trauma.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I will read excerpts, which Members can follow in the distributed report. “On 15 September 2017, Sergeant Chan, who was participating in 'Exercise Wallaby', an annual unilateral training exercise conducted by the Singapore Armed Forces at Shoalwater Bay Training Area in Queensland died after the infantry vehicle (known as the Bionix) he was commanding rolled and he suffered significant injuries.

sections.label: Police view and SAF recommendation
sections.summary: Police considered the incident likely due to the commander's reversal decision and exposed body position; SAF recommends only head and shoulders outside the turret.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The police considered that it was likely that the incident occurred because of the commander’s decision to reverse on a slightly different path down the hill and that his choice to be positioned with part of his body outside the vehicle exposed him to greater risk of injury.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The Singapore Armed Forces recommendation is only the head and shoulders be outside the turret of the vehicle during operations.

sections.label: Committee of Inquiry corroborates Queensland findings
sections.summary: The Committee of Inquiry, appointed by the Armed Forces Council, corroborated the Queensland authorities' findings from its own investigation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The Committee of Inquiry here, appointed by the Armed Forces Council, corroborated from their own investigation the findings by the Queensland authorities.

sections.label: Night vision device not working
sections.summary: The night vision device of 3SG Chan's vehicle was not working.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: First, the night vision device (NVD) of 3SG Chan’s vehicle was not working.

sections.label: COI findings and training safety recommendation
sections.summary: The COI found no negligence, foul play or misconduct, but recommended the SAF review training safety regulations on the Armoured Fighting Vehicle Commander's position.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The COI also found no negligence, foul play or misconduct, but recommended that the SAF review its training safety regulations on the position of the Armoured Fighting Vehicle Commander, so that the vehicle commander is able to execute the overturning drill, which means that he is able to drop quickly into the vehicle.

sections.label: Training safety regulations tightened
sections.summary: Training safety regulations have been tightened to limit exposure of the vehicle commander's body to waist level during certain operational tasks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Training safety regulations (TSRs) have been tightened to limit exposure of the body of the vehicle commander to waist level when executing certain operational tasks.

sections.label: Corporal Lee heat injury after march
sections.summary: On 18 April this year, Corporal Lee displayed signs of heat injury after completing an eight-kilometre fast march in Bedok Camp.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: On 18 April this year, Corporal Lee displayed signs of heat injury after completing an eight-kilometre fast march in Bedok Camp.

sections.label: Corporal Lee passed away at CGH
sections.summary: Corporal Lee's condition deteriorated and he passed away on 30 April 2018 at CGH, about 12 days after admission.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Unfortunately, Corporal Lee's condition deteriorated and he passed away on 30 April 2018 at CGH, about 12 days after his admission.

sections.label: SAF heat injuries and deaths
sections.summary: The SAF has had no heat stroke deaths since 2009, but heat injuries occur each year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: While the SAF has not had any death from heat stroke since 2009, heat injuries do occur each year.

sections.label: Heat injury prevention guidelines
sections.summary: Guidelines include mandatory water parades and barring soldiers with temperatures above 37.5oC from training.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: These guidelines formed the regimes which I have just mentioned against heat injuries and they include mandatory water parades before, during and after a training activity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We take temperature before the training and any soldier with a temperature above 37.5oC is not allowed to train.

sections.label: Heat injury measures and review
sections.summary: The SAF is evaluating wearable monitoring devices and MINDEF will commission an External Medical Panel to review heat injury management.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Our commanders, soldiers, regulars, Full-time National Servicemen (NSFs) and Operationally Ready National Servicemen (NSmen) know from their own experience that it is the consistent practice for these processes and precautions to be carried out.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We must press on to achieve zero fatalities from heat injuries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The SAF is currently evaluating the use of individual wearable devices to monitor a soldier’s condition real-time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: MINDEF will also commission an External Medical Panel, as we did in 2010, to review the SAF's policies and measures for the management of heat injuries and recommend improvements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This panel should consider further steps, especially when recorded temperatures in Singapore over the last two decades have gone up, increasing the risk of heat injuries.

sections.label: Convictions over training deaths
sections.summary: A Conducting Officer was jailed six months, and officers in a 2005 trainee death got six to 12 months.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The Conducting Officer who appointed a serviceman to drive the military vehicle even though the Conducting Officer knew that the serviceman did not have a military driving licence was convicted in the criminal Courts and sentenced to six months' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In 2005, the Supervising Officer, Conducting Officer and instructors who were involved in the death of a trainee who was submerged in water during a Combat Survival Training course were sentenced to six to 12 months' imprisonment.

sections.label: External Review Panel role
sections.summary: An ERPSS member will join COIs for training-related deaths, and the ERPSS will publicly report on COI findings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: These are qualified eminent members and I would like this External Review Panel to do more.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So, for a start, MINDEF has discussed with the Chairman of the ERPSS who has agreed to include one of their members in the COIs for all training-related deaths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In addition, the COI will now submit its full report to the ERPSS for further questions, comments and views.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In turn, the ERPSS will provide a written report on the COI findings which will be made public.

sections.label: NS training death rates
sections.summary: Over two decades there was about one NS training-related death a year, with none from 2013 to 2016.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Over the last two decades, we have had, on average, about one NS training-related death a year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: From 2013 to 2016 we had no NS training deaths, four years, none.

sections.label: Commanders and zero training fatalities
sections.summary: Commanders take this trust seriously and will do their best to achieve zero fatalities in training.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Our commanders take this seriously and never take this trust for granted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We will do our very best to achieve zero fatalities in training.

sections.label: Abuse of power by commanders
sections.summary: Members or the public can report abuse of power and unfair treatment, and commanders who abuse authority or breach training safety will be punished.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: If any Member of this House or any member of the public can give me details that there has been abuse of power and that recruits have been unfairly treated, let me know.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But that does not give any excuse to any commander to abuse his position, to abuse his authority to do over and beyond what is necessary.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: If it is not safe for whatever reason, even well-intentioned, it is wrong.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: If you expose people to unsafe practices, go against training safety regulations, you are wrong from the outset.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And if you do not know how to protect the men, then I say you cannot be a good commander.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: It is behaviour prejudicial to good order and you do not deserve to be a commander and you will be punished accordingly.

sections.label: SCDF and Home Team rules review
sections.summary: SCDF and other Home Team agencies are directed to relook at rules, focus on enforcement and come up with further measures by next week.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They trust us and we have to maintain that trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, I have directed SCDF as well as the other Home Team agencies to relook at the rules, how they are enforced, focus on the enforcement, come up with a further set of measures by next week.

sections.label: Night armour training safety and COI
sections.summary: Night armour training requires night vision devices or open hatch and lights, and the COI will submit its full report to the External Review Panel on SAF Safety, which will write a public report.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The training safety regulations for armour training at night require you to use night vision devices and, exactly for the purpose where you have poor visibility, you need to see where you are moving.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: You can move without night vision devices if you have, as I have said, the hatch open and the lights on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: It is the responsibility of the vehicle commander to report if his night vision devices are not working and, whereupon, you stop the exercise for safety purposes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But by and large, I think we should be prepared to give out as much information.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: That is the reason why we have said that the External Review Panel on SAF Safety will be a member of the COI.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The COI will submit the full report to the External Review Panel for their questions, for their comments and views.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: This External Review Panel for safety will write a report and that will be made public.

sections.label: Training safety regulations benefit soldier
sections.summary: Training safety regulations are written to give the benefit of the doubt to the individual soldier.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The way our training safety regulations are written, they give the benefit of the doubt to the individual soldier.

sections.label: Assurance to parents of dead servicemen
sections.summary: Parents of any National Serviceman who has died are assured all facts will be established and those responsible punished, without a witch hunt for honest mistakes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And if they had said no, then I would have to rely just to release to this House our COI report because, that coroner's report, by Queensland's procedures, is only given to the parents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We want to assure the parents of any unfortunate National Serviceman who has died, that all the facts will be fully established.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Anyone held responsible that deserves punishment will get punished.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Neither should we go on a witch hunt, if they are honest mistakes, because the commanders are someone else's son, too, National Servicemen.

sections.label: Safety, duty, abuse punishment
sections.summary: States that safety comes first, members must do their job, and abuse of position will be punished.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Safety first, do your job, if you abuse your position, you will be punished.

sections.label: COI and Police report temperature
sections.summary: Says the COI and Police report should disregard it, as he had a normal temperature before the activity started.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The COI and Police report should disregard it as this is what we found.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: He was found to have a normal temperature before the activity started.

sections.label: Choosing National Servicemen commanders
sections.summary: Describes choosing commanders through psychological tests, peer appraisal, and screening out those unfit to lead.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: So, we have to make sure that for our National Servicemen, the commanders are well chosen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We have psychological tests, to the extent possible, they weed out those who have mal-adjusted attributes, that are not fit to lead.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: In addition, peer appraisal plays a very important role.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And if your peers think that you are not fit to lead, that you do not have enough empathy, or that you do not listen, or that you do not have enough command presence or command ability, then we do not choose you.

sections.label: External Review Panel information access
sections.summary: Says the full COI will be given to the External Review Panel, with security elements largely maintained.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: For the External Review Panel, yes, the full COI will be given to them so that they can assess the information and ask more questions and, from that, write their report.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But, by and large, in many instances, the security elements can be maintained.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And I would give as much information to this House, to the External Review Panel that you want, so that they, too, can come to an independent conclusion.

sections.label: Army safety timeout after incident
sections.summary: Says the Army leadership mobilised quickly, stopped and paused all activities for a safety timeout.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: When this incident occurred, the Army was mobilised very quickly at the top leadership levels.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We stopped, had a safety timeout for all activities; paused, everybody stopped, safety first.

sections.label: Army Commanders engage unit and family
sections.summary: Says Army Commanders went down to engage the men, the deceased's family, and his platoon mates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: For that individual unit, the Army Commanders went down, engaged the men, engaged the family members of the deceased CFC Dave Lee, as well as what the Member has rightly pointed out, how it would affect his platoon mates.

sections.label: Zero-fatality system goal
sections.summary: No one can guarantee no such incident will occur in another period, time or unit, but the aim is a zero-fatality system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Because no one can guarantee you that no such incident will occur in another period, in another time, in another unit.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: We will do our level best to get a zero-fatality system.

sections.label: One death a year average
sections.summary: On average, there is one death a year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: As I have said, on average, we have one death a year.
